test_title: PYST 4: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Lion Capital located at Sarnath, which is adopted as the national emblem of the Republic of India, was erected by which of the following Mauryan kings?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lion Capital at Sarnath** was erected by **Emperor Ashoka** during his reign in the **3rd century BCE.**
 
• It is located at **Sarnath**, near **Varanasi**, in the modern-day state of **Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• The Lion Capital was originally placed atop the **Ashokan Pillar**, which is a monolithic column made of polished sandstone.
 
• The capital features **four Asiatic lions** seated back-to-back, symbolizing **power, courage, pride, and confidence**.
 
• The base of the Lion Capital includes a circular abacus adorned with sculptures of **elephants, horses, bulls, and lions**, separated by **spoked wheels (Dharma Chakra)**.
 
• The **National Emblem of India**, adopted on **26 January 1950**, is an adaptation of this Lion Capital. It excludes the fourth lion and the bell-shaped lotus base.
 
• The Lion Capital symbolizes the spread of the **Dharma (righteousness)** and the values of **peace, non-violence, and justice** as propagated by Ashoka following his conversion to Buddhism.
 
• *Hence, Ashoka is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Emperor Ashoka:**

 
 
• **Ashoka** was the third ruler of the **Mauryan Empire** and is regarded as one of the greatest emperors in Indian history.
 
• He reigned from **268 BCE to 232 BCE** and played a key role in spreading **Buddhism** across India and other parts of Asia.
 
• Ashoka's transformation from a conqueror to a proponent of peace occurred after the **Kalinga War**, which caused immense suffering.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Lion Capital:**
 
 
• The Lion Capital represents **Buddhist ideals**, including the promotion of harmony, justice, and moral governance.
 
• It was installed at Sarnath, the site where **Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon**, known as the **Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta**.
 
 
 
• **Other Ashokan Pillars:**
 
 
• Ashoka commissioned numerous pillars across his empire, many of which feature inscriptions detailing his **edicts and policies**.
 
• These pillars are made of **polished sandstone** and are remarkable for their architectural precision and craftsmanship.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Adoption of the National Emblem:**

 
 
• The Government of India adopted the **Lion Capital** as the **National Emblem** on **26 January 1950**, the day India became a **Republic**.
 
• The motto "**Satyameva Jayate**" (Truth Alone Triumphs), derived from the **Mundaka Upanishad**, is inscribed below the emblem.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Bindusara:** The father of Ashoka, he was the second Mauryan emperor but is not associated with the Lion Capital.
 
• **Devavarman Maurya:** A later Mauryan ruler with no known contributions to monumental architecture like the Lion Capital.
 
• **Samprati Maurya:** A successor of Ashoka, known for promoting Jainism rather than Buddhism.
